## ARS Desktop App (Tauri / Windows, Mac, Linux)

This wraps the existing ARS web app in a real native desktop window using
[Tauri](https://tauri.app). Same idea as the mobile app in `../mobile-app/` — it's a thin
native shell that loads your live server, not a rebuild of any app logic.

Lives in `desktop-app/` alongside the main PHP project and the Capacitor mobile app.

**Heads up:** these files were hand-written rather than generated by `cargo tauri init`,
because the environment they were scaffolded in doesn't have Rust installed. The structure
follows current Tauri v2 conventions closely, but **hasn't been build-tested** — the first
`cargo tauri build` on your machine is the real verification. If something doesn't resolve
cleanly, cross-check against [tauri.app](https://tauri.app) or paste me the error.

---

### ⚠️ Before you build: the same certificate requirement as mobile

Exactly the same issue as `../mobile-app/CAPACITOR.md`: Tauri's webview does not offer a
"click through" option for self-signed certificates the way a normal browser tab does.
`tauri.conf.json`'s `app.windows[0].url` needs to point at a server with a **real, trusted**
HTTPS certificate — see the Tailscale HTTPS Certificates section in `../TAILSCALE.md`.

---

### Project structure

```
desktop-app/
├── package.json
└── src-tauri/
    ├── Cargo.toml
    ├── build.rs
    ├── tauri.conf.json     ← set your server URL here (see warning above)
    ├── capabilities/
    │   └── default.json     (baseline permissions only — no filesystem/shell access granted)
    ├── icons/                (Windows .ico + PNGs ready; macOS .icns still needed — see below)
    └── src/
        ├── main.rs
        └── lib.rs
```

---

### One-time setup (on your own machine)

You'll need:
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org)
- [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) (via `rustup`)
- Platform build tools:
  - **Windows:** "Desktop development with C++" workload from Visual Studio Build Tools
  - **Mac:** Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`)
  - **Linux:** see [Tauri's Linux prerequisites](https://tauri.app/start/prerequisites/)

```bash
cd desktop-app
npm install
```

Edit `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and replace the placeholder URL in `app.windows[0].url`
with your real, trusted-HTTPS address.

---

### macOS icon

`icons/icon.icns` isn't included — generating a real one needs either a Mac or the Tauri
CLI itself (Rust wasn't available where this was built). Once Rust is installed, regenerate
the whole icon set properly from the 1024×1024 source in `../mobile-app/assets/icon-only.png`:

```bash
cargo install tauri-cli --version "^2"
cargo tauri icon ../mobile-app/assets/icon-only.png
```

This overwrites everything in `src-tauri/icons/` with a complete, correct set (including a
real `.icns`) generated from that one source image — safe to run even though the `.ico` and
PNGs already here are already valid.

---

### Running & building

```bash
cd desktop-app

# Dev mode — opens a window, hot-reloads on config changes
npm run dev

# Production build — produces a real installer for your current OS
# (.exe/.msi on Windows, .dmg/.app on Mac, .deb/.AppImage on Linux)
npm run build
```

Output lands in `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`.

---

### What this does *not* do

- No offline support — thin shell over your live server, same as the mobile app and the PWA.
- No custom native features wired in (file system access, native menus, tray icon, etc.).
  `capabilities/default.json` intentionally grants only the baseline permissions Tauri needs
  to run a window — nothing privileged. Ask if you want any native capabilities added.
- Only builds for whichever OS you run `npm run build` on — there's no cross-compiling a
  Windows `.exe` from a Mac (or vice versa) without extra toolchain setup.
